# Dockerfile for lammps-reax on CPU
# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, well-supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Define reusable environment variables for directories
ENV LAMMPS_SRC_DIR=/usr/src/lammps
ENV LAMMPS_INSTALL_DIR=/opt/lammps

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes
# This prevents errors related to shared memory (vader) and high-speed interconnects (openib)
# and allows oversubscribing processes to cores, a common container pattern.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# Install dependencies, clone, build, and install LAMMPS in a single RUN layer
# This approach helps to keep the Docker image size smaller.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    ca-certificates \
    # FIX: Add python3, which is a build dependency for modern LAMMPS versions
    python3 && \
    # Clone the latest branch of the LAMMPS source code
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git ${LAMMPS_SRC_DIR} && \
    # Create build directory and change into it
    mkdir -p ${LAMMPS_SRC_DIR}/build && \
    cd ${LAMMPS_SRC_DIR}/build && \
    # Configure the LAMMPS build with CMake
    # Enable the REAXFF package as required for this application
    cmake ../cmake \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
        -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=${LAMMPS_INSTALL_DIR} && \
    # Compile LAMMPS using all available processor cores
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Install the compiled binaries and libraries
    make install && \
    # Create the working directory for the final image
    mkdir -p /data && \
    # Copy the required example files into the working directory
    cp ${LAMMPS_SRC_DIR}/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /data/ && \
    # Clean up to minimize final image size by removing the source code
    rm -rf ${LAMMPS_SRC_DIR} && \
    # Clean up the apt cache to further reduce image size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Add the LAMMPS installation directory to the system PATH
# This makes the 'lmp' executable available globally.
ENV PATH=${LAMMPS_INSTALL_DIR}/bin:${PATH}

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /data

# Default command to start an interactive shell.
# The container can be run with `docker run -it <image> lmp -in <input_script>`
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

#
# MiniCluster manifest for running a LAMMPS ReaxFF experiment.
#
# This manifest defines a Flux Operator MiniCluster to run a specific
# LAMMPS simulation. It is configured to run on a single node within
# a Kubernetes cluster, suitable for an AWS CPU instance environment.
#
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: lammps-reaxff-hns-experiment
  # Deploy to the default namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Specify the size of the MiniCluster, which corresponds to the number of pods.
  # Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of tasks for the job. Flux will run the command with `flux run -n <tasks>`.
  # For this single-process command, we set tasks to 1.
  tasks: 1

  # The application container that runs the LAMMPS simulation.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to execute. The Flux Operator will wrap this with `flux run`.
      # It runs the specified LAMMPS input file.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This container is a worker, not the one that launches the MiniCluster setup.
      launcher: false

  # Logging mode for the Flux Operator.
  # Strict mode will fail the job if there are any logging errors.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod cleanup policy.
  # Setting to false prevents the pods from being deleted after the job completes,
  # which is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

#
# MiniCluster manifest for running a LAMMPS ReaxFF experiment, corrected for resource allocation.
#
# This manifest has been updated to resolve a Flux resource allocation error.
# The number of tasks is set to 63 on a 64-vCPU node to reserve one CPU for the Flux broker.
# The LAMMPS command is adjusted to use a processor grid (7x3x3) that matches the 63 tasks.
#
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lmp-reaxff-hns-experiment-corrected
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The job runs on a single pod.
  size: 1

  # FIX: Reduced tasks from 64 to 63. The c6a.16xlarge instance has 64 vCPUs,
  # but the Flux broker requires one CPU, leaving 63 available for the job.
  # Requesting all 64 CPUs caused an "unsatisfiable request" allocation error from Flux.
  tasks: 63

  # Using the standard jobspec field to define pod attributes for v1alpha2.
  jobspec:
    template:
      spec:
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "c6a.16xlarge"

  logging:
    strict: true
  cleanup: false

  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The main container does not launch the MPI tasks; Flux does.
      launcher: false
      # FIX: The LAMMPS processor grid variables (x, y, z) must multiply
      # to equal the number of tasks. This is updated to 7x3x3 to match the 63 tasks.
      command: lmp -v x 7 -v y 3 -v z 3 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

#
# Corrected MiniCluster manifest for LAMMPS ReaxFF experiment.
#
# This manifest fixes the "unknown field 'spec.jobspec'" error by moving
# pod-level specifications like nodeSelector and restartPolicy to the correct
# 'spec.pod' field, as required by the v1alpha2 API. It also includes
# additional requested settings like backoffLimit and restartPolicy.
#
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Using a descriptive name for the corrected experiment.
  name: lmp-reaxff-hns-experiment-corrected
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size corresponds to the number of pods in the MiniCluster, limited to one node.
  size: 1
  # Tasks defines the total number of MPI ranks for the job.
  tasks: 63

  # Set backoffLimit to 1 to prevent retries on failure, allowing for faster debugging cycles.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # All containers for the job are defined here.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      command: lmp -v x 7 -v y 3 -v z 3 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # launcher=false indicates this is the main application container.
      launcher: false

  # Pod-specific configurations are nested under the 'pod' field.
  pod:
    # Set restartPolicy to Never so logs from failed pods can be inspected.
    restartPolicy: Never
    # FIX: The nodeSelector was incorrectly placed under a non-existent 'spec.jobspec' field.
    # It has been moved to the correct location at 'spec.pod.nodeSelector' per the CRD definition.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "c6a.16xlarge"

The previous runs on a 64-core ARM instance resulted in a 28s wall time. This attempt will test a high-performance Intel instance (c6i.16xlarge) to compare architectural performance. The task count is set to 32 to match the number of physical cores, as HPC workloads often perform better without hyper-threading.

Previous results show the 64-core ARM instance (27s) significantly outperformed the 64-vCPU Intel instance (47s). This attempt tests the AMD architecture equivalent (c6a.16xlarge, 64-vCPU) to determine the best x86 platform. The task count is set to 64 to utilize all available vCPUs via hyper-threading, mirroring the most successful configuration so far.

The ARM-based hpc7g.16xlarge instance with 64 tasks yielded the best performance at 27s. Subsequent tests on different x86 architectures (Intel, AMD) resulted in significantly longer wall times. The application appears highly optimized for the Graviton architecture, and further significant improvements are unlikely. Reverting to the best-known configuration for the final run.
